content: The equivalence harness's creation-order ledger (eq/adapters/orchestrator.py _capture) diffs each checkpoint's id set against the PRE-RUN baseline (get_state before setup). summary: Ledger baseline is pre-setup; stale SH3D driver state makes created-lists lose reused ids and IdMap rotates homely's correct ids into phantom diffs.

title: SH3D export parity: angles wrap to [-180,180); wallsAlpha is transparency not opacity
content: Two parity details from B8 that are easy to get wrong when matching the SH3D Java driver's state export: (1) Angle export wraps into [-180, 180), not (-180, 180] — yaw π must export as -180.0, because SH3D Camera.yaw is a float and Math.toDegrees(float-π) lands slightly above 180, so the driver's `deg % 360; if (deg > 180) deg -= 360` pushes it negative before round3. Implement `n >= 180 → n -= 360`. (2) HomeEnvironment.wallsAlpha is a TRANSPARENCY (Wall3D.java:1522 passes it straight to Java3D
summary: Driver angle wrap is [-180,180) (yaw pi -> -180.0) and wallsAlpha is transparency (0=opaque), plus fovDeg never wraps

title: SH3D compass Etc/GMT/UTC entry is Greenwich Observatory (51.466667,0)deg, NOT (0,0)
content: Ticket B8 (homely export-parity-defaults) kickoff text and docs/behaviours/sh3d-camera-and-export.md §3 both state "UTC/Greenwich/Etc/GMT → (0,0)". The actual SH3D 7.5 source (sweethome3d-7.5-wayland-patch/src/com/eteks/sweethome3d/model/Compass.java:673) defines `greenwich = new GeographicPoint(51.466667f, 0f)` and maps Etc/GMT, GMT, Greenwich, UCT, UTC, Universal, WET, Zulu to it. So a machine set to UTC exports compass latitudeRad round3(toRadians(51.466667f)) ≈ 0.898, longitudeRad 0 — not 0/
summary: SH3D Compass.java maps UTC/Etc/GMT to Greenwich Observatory (51.466667, 0), not (0,0) as the B8 ticket/contract doc claim

title: SH3D top-camera bounds require mitered thick-polygon wall corners
content: SH3D top-camera bounds use MITERED wall outlines, not plain thick rectangles: Wall.getShapePoints() moves cap corners of joined walls to the intersection of their side lines (same-side pairing for chain joins, opposite for head-on), clamped to 2*max thickness. An L-shaped chain therefore shifts the union bounds center off-axis: walls (100,100)-(600,100) plus (600,100)-(600,400), thickness 7, give center x=(100+603.5)/2=351.75 (not 350). Any port that skips miters fails the numeric verification t
summary: SH3D camera bounds miter joined wall corners; naive rectangles break the verification table

title: Harness deep-diff treats JSON null == absent key; remaining live-run diffs are genuine B7/B8 gaps
content: The SH3D driver golden export serializes "no value" as explicit JSON null while the homely export omits the key entirely (home name, walls[*] arcExtent/heightAtEnd/levelRef/leftSideColor/rightSideColor, cameras.*.fixedSize etc.). Since harness commit b0a7501 (C8) the deep-diff treats absent key == null value in both directions at every level, so these no longer produce state-diff failures. BUT genuine value differences still fail: live run 20260826-105922 replay leaves 18 real parity gaps owned

title: py3.12 asyncio.Server.wait_closed() blocks until client connections close
content:
Python 3.12 changed `asyncio.Server.wait_closed()` to wait until all existing client connections finish, not just for the listener to close. In-process test fakes that wrap `asyncio.start_server` must track writer objects and explicitly close them during teardown before calling `wait_closed()`, otherwise tests hang indefinitely while a client keeps its socket open.

Related: when wrapping framed transports behind `eq.adapters.server.Session` (equivalence harness), pass a send_fn and feed inbound
summary: py3.12 asyncio.Server.wait_closed() blocks on live connections; fakes must close tracked writers

title: Co-committing entangled WIP: checkout-to-HEAD + reapply-own-hunks + restore-combined pattern
content: When two agents' uncommitted WIP entangles in shared files (here: homely-handler.ts held B5's screenshot wiring mixed with B3's broken plan bits), do NOT commit the merged blob and do NOT wait indefinitely. Working pattern: (1) save the combined file to /tmp/opencode/<name>-combined.ts; (2) `git checkout HEAD -- <shared files>` to get a pristine base; (3) re-apply ONLY your own hunks plus the minimal fixes needed for green state (document them in the commit body — folding another agent's obvious
summary: Entangled WIP co-commit: checkout shared files to HEAD, re-apply only your hunks + minimal green-state fixes, stage explicitly, then restore combined file to preserve teammate WIP

summary: SH3D materializes in-progress walls into the home during drawing; buffered clones must add pending endpoints to snap candidates

title: Observe a subscription-less store by shadowing instance methods and restoring originals (never delete)
content: homely/src/core/store.ts HomeStore is intentionally pure with NO subscription mechanism, and the file belongs to another task's scope (B2), so it must not be modified. homely/src/view3d/watch.ts solves live-sync by shadowing INSTANCE methods: capture bound originals of apply/undo/redo/resetToEmpty, replace them on the instance with wrappers that call the original then notify listeners (undo/redo notify only when they actually changed state, checked via return value/canRedo delta), and restore th
summary: Subscription shim for pure stores: shadow instance methods with bound originals, restore on unobserve without delete

title: Adding an automation command requires updating handshake.test.ts expected commands array
content: HomelyCommandHandler.get_capabilities spreads its `commands` tuple, so adding any command silently changes the ARRAY LENGTH returned to clients. tests/handshake.test.ts asserts the full expected commands array via toMatchObject — with arrays, toMatchObject requires EXACT length match, so every new automation command must also be appended to that test's expected list or the handshake suite fails. Hit when B4 added 'set_camera'/'camera_preset'; will recur for every future command addition.
summary: get_capabilities test uses exact-length array match — every new command must update tests/handshake.test.ts expected list

title: SH3D 3D world maps plan coords directly: (x, height, y), camera rotation.y = π − rad(yaw), rotation.x = −rad(pitch)
content: Sweet Home 3D's HomeComponent3D.updateViewPlatformTransform builds R = RotY(π − yaw)·RotX(−pitch) and translates to (cameraX, cameraZ, cameraY) — meaning the 3D world IS plan space: x_plan→x, z(height)→y, y_plan→z, with NO z mirroring. In Three.js terms: `camera.position.set(cam.x, cam.z, cam.y); camera.rotation.order='YXZ'; rotation.y = Math.PI − degToRad(cam.yawDeg); rotation.x = −degToRad(cam.pitchDeg)`. Wall segments use yaw = atan2(yEnd−yStart, xEnd−xStart) DIRECTLY as their Y rotation in t
summary: SH3D world mapping: (x_plan, z_height, y_plan), camera rotY(π−yaw)·RotX(−pitch), wall yaw=atan2(dy,dx) — no z-mirror

title: SH3D undoManager is private — read canUndo/canRedo via cached reflective Field
content:
In SH3D 7.5, `HomeController.undoManager` is private with no accessor, but the protocol needs `capabilities.canUndo/canRedo`. Solution used by the Java driver (`InteractionCommands.java`, equivalence/driver-java): cache a `java.lang.reflect.Field` for `HomeController.undoManager` once in a static initializer with `setAccessible(true)`, then read it per call and query `canUndo()`/`canRedo()` on the UndoManager.

This works from the unnamed module WITHOUT `--add-opens` JVM flags (the target class
summary: Read undoManager capabilities via cached reflective Field (no --add-opens needed)

title: SH3D default Home contains zero Level objects — export levels as [] with null levelRefs
content:
Fresh `createHome()` in Sweet Home 3D 7.5 returns a Home whose `getLevels()` is **empty** and where every item's `getLevel()` is `null`. There is no implicit default Level object.

For NormalizedHomeState export (schema v1) the correct output is therefore `levels: []` with all `levelRef` fields `null` — the schema's `$defs.ref` treats null as "implicit level 0". Do NOT synthesize a placeholder Level during export: it would create spurious diffs against Homely if the clone models the implicit gro
summary: SH3D fresh Home has zero Levels; export levels:[] with null levelRef

title: SH3D paste/cut mutate the passed items — clipboard must deep-copy (serialize) or undo semantics break
content: HomeController.paste(items)/cut(items) add and move THE OBJECTS PASSED IN — no copying. A driver clipboard that stores live references to selected model objects makes paste re-add the very same Wall objects (home list holds duplicate references) and moveItems(+20cm) mutates the originals; undo then removes the wrong edit and coordinates are silently offset. Fix used in sh3d-driver: clipboard stored as Java-serialized bytes (ObjectOutputStream over the List<Selectable>), thawed on paste — exactly
summary: controller.paste(live refs) aliases walls and corrupts undo — clipboard must deep-copy via Java serialization

title: SH3D wall loop: click start point first, then double_click joins — bare double_click creates a diagonal
content: In Sweet Home 3D's wall state machine, `double_click` (PlanController.pressMouse with clickCount=2) does NOT commit the in-progress wall — it joins the LAST COMMITTED wall's end to the nearest existing wall endpoint at the cursor, moving that endpoint. Driving a closed room with N corners via move+click per corner + double_click on the start point therefore produces a DIAGONAL wall (the previous wall's end gets dragged to the start point) instead of the closing segment. summary: Wall-loop close needs click on start point BEFORE double_click; bare double_click drags previous wall's end (diagonal)

Tauri v2 Linux builds require libdbus-1-dev + full WebKitGTK dev stack; generate_context! needs icons/icon.png even with empty bundle.icon
content:
Building any Tauri v2 app on Debian/Ubuntu Linux fails with three distinct errors if system packages are missing:

1. `libdbus-sys` build.rs panics with an explicit message when `libdbus-1-dev` is absent — install it first; it is not pulled in by the webkit/gtk metapackages listed in Tauri docs.
2. `pkg-config` errors like `Package libsoup-3.0 was not found` mean the GTK/WebKit dev stack is missing: `libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libgtk-3-dev libsoup-3.0-dev libjavascriptcoregtk-4.1-dev libxdo-dev libss
summary: Tauri v2 on Linux needs libdbus-1-dev plus WebKitGTK dev stack; generate_context! always demands icons/icon.png

title: Bare `on:`/`off:` keys parse as YAML 1.1 booleans under PyYAML
content:
PyYAML implements YAML 1.1, where bare unquoted `on:` / `off:` / `yes:` / `no:` keys and values parse as booleans. In equivalence scenario YAMLs an assertion field literally named `on:` became key `True`, producing the confusing pydantic error "Keys should be strings" instead of anything mentioning `on`.

Decision (ticket c1-dsl): eq.dsl.schema.Assertion uses `artifact:` (`state|plan|3d`) instead of `on`. Any future YAML contract in this repo (scenario DSL, equivalence/matrix/features.yaml, beha
summary: PyYAML parses bare `on:`/`off:` keys as booleans; DSL uses `artifact:` instead of `on`.

title: Comparators match objects by ledger creation order — never by literal adapter ids
content: In house_designer's equivalence harness, adapters (sh3d-driver, homely) mint their own opaque object ids, so comparators must NEVER compare ids literally across adapters. `eq/comparators/match.py` build_id_map pairs objects by creation order recorded in the orchestrator's ledger.json ({adapter, step, created:{coll:[ids]}, removed:{...}}): levels pair positionally, collections by ledger ordinals → identical-id fallback → leftover zip. IdMap.rewrite_actual() renames actual-state ids/levelRef/selec
summary: Cross-adapter objects match by ledger creation order; ids are never compared literally
